transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, it's mostly because of some things at work. I teach at a secondary school, and... I just haven't been able to shake this feeling lately. 

It's about the staff emails, mostly. And the morning announcements. It feels like... well, like they're actually coded messages directed at me. Some of my colleagues have gently tried to show me that they're just standard messages sent to everyone on staff, but... I don't know. I just can't seem to shake the feeling that they're about me.
Besides these feelings about the messages, have you been hearing voices or sounds that others around you don't seem to hear?

I... suppose so. Just occasionally. 

Um, mostly when it's very quiet. Like after the students leave for the day, or... at home. I'll hear a woman's voice. She just... says my name, usually. Or makes a brief comment about whatever I'm doing. It sounds perfectly clear, so... I usually answer her before I realize that I'm completely alone in the room.

Over the past few weeks or months, have you noticed any periods where you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt energetic and productive, or times when your thoughts were racing or you felt unusually energized?

Um... no. I don't think so. 

My sleep hasn't really changed. And I haven't felt... unusually energized or anything like that. Just... normal, I suppose.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings that the messages are directed at you and hearing the woman's voice? Has it been going on continuously for weeks or months?

Um... I suppose it's been a while now. 

Maybe... about four months? Yes, around four months that I've noticed the messages... and the voice. It's just been going on since then.
Over these past four months, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your job as a teacher, or in your relationships with colleagues and friends?

I'm... still teaching. It's mostly fine. I suppose I have needed... a little help from my coworkers lately. Just covering parts of the project lessons, or... getting through some of our planning meetings. 

And socially... I guess I haven't been very reliable. I've stopped going to my book club... and the theater, and... neighborhood things. I just... haven't been going.

When you first started noticing these things about the messages and hearing the voice four months ago, did it come on suddenly over days or a week or so, or did it develop more gradually over a longer period before you really noticed it?
I'm... not really sure. It's hard to say, exactly. I just... realized it was happening at some point. I didn't really keep track of how it started.
Besides the changes you mentioned at work and socially, have you noticed any changes in how you take care of yourself — like your hygiene, or the way you dress, or keeping your living space clean?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I still get up and get dressed for work every day. My house is... it's fine. Just the usual. I haven't really noticed anything different with that.

Looking back to around four months ago when this started, was there anything significant happening in your life at that time — like a major stressful event, loss, or significant change — that seemed to come before you noticed these feelings about the messages and hearing the voice?
I don't... I don't think so. There wasn't anything like that. Just... normal life, really. Nothing stands out.
Over these four months, have the messages you're receiving and the voice you're hearing stayed about the same, or have they gotten noticeably worse or more intense?
I suppose they've mostly... stayed the same. I haven't really noticed them getting worse or anything. They're just... there. I don't really know how else to describe it.
Have you noticed any changes in the way you speak or think — like your thoughts feeling jumbled or hard to follow, or people telling you that what you're saying doesn't make sense?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I teach all day, so people seem to understand me just fine. No one has said I don't make sense. My thoughts are just... normal. I haven't noticed any problem.

Have you ever found yourself doing things that seemed strange or unusual to you, or have people commented that your behavior seemed odd or didn't make sense — apart from the messages and the voice we've already discussed?

I... well, sometimes. Just small things. Like during my lessons, or when we have the art-fair meetings... I might stop what I'm doing. Just to... arrange the markers on the desk. Or the papers. They just have to be in a certain pattern. And sometimes I... I might just repeat what someone else just said, instead of answering them. I don't really know why I do it. It's a bit embarrassing, really, because it stops the lesson. But... I try not to let it happen too much.

When you repeat what someone else just said instead of answering them — does that happen often during conversations, or is it mainly just during those specific moments like the art-fair meetings you mentioned?

Mostly just... during those times. The lessons or the meetings. I'll just catch myself doing it... repeating a phrase instead of responding normally. Or stopping mid-task to fix the papers like I said. It doesn't happen all the time. It just... it interrupts what I'm supposed to be doing. Which is... well, embarrassing. I try to just move on.

When you're talking with your colleagues or teaching your students, do you find that your emotions come through naturally — like smiling when something is funny, or showing concern when someone is upset — or do people sometimes comment that you seem emotionally flat or distant?

I don't think anyone has said I seem flat. I... I still care about my students. And my friends. It's just... 

I guess for a long time now, maybe months, I just feel... drained. Like the warmth is gone. I don't really do much anymore. I stopped going to my book club. I used to help plan the local theater stuff, but I let that slide too. Even just... answering the phone. I don't really do it unless someone pushes me. I just... don't have the drive for it.

When you think back to before these four months started, would you say you were more active and engaged with your hobbies and social life — like going to the book club and theater regularly — or had you already been pulling back from those things gradually over a longer period?

I suppose... it wasn't just four months ago. The pulling back, I mean. It's been... longer. Since my youngest moved away for college. That was about... a year and two months ago, maybe? That's when everything just started to... shift. How I work, how I am with people... it's all been different since then.

So when your youngest moved away about a year ago, you started feeling more withdrawn and drained. But the feeling that the emails were coded messages about you — that started about four months ago, correct? So there was roughly an eight-month period where you were feeling drained and pulling back, but you weren't yet noticing the messages or hearing the voice?
Yes... I suppose so. The things with the messages... and the voice. That's only been going on for about four months. Before that, it was just... what we talked about. The pulling back.

When you think about these coded messages in the emails and announcements — do you have a sense of what the messages mean or what purpose they're serving? Like, do you think someone is trying to tell you something specific, or warn you about something, or are they more just confusing and hard to make sense of?
I... I don't really know. It's just... they're there. I don't know what they want. It's just... confusing.

When you think about your day-to-day experience over these past four months, would you say the biggest problem has been the confusion about the coded messages and the voice, or has it been more the times when you find yourself repeating things or arranging things in patterns instead of doing what you're supposed to be doing?

I suppose... it's the other things. I don't really like talking about it. 

It's just... at school. During my lessons, or sometimes in the art-fair meetings. I'll just stop right in the middle of what I'm doing. I catch myself... rearranging my whiteboard markers, or lining up papers in a... a very specific pattern. Or someone will say something, and I'll just repeat their phrase back to them instead of answering normally. 

It's... it's just very embarrassing. Because it interrupts what I'm actually supposed to be doing. So... yes, I guess that part is the biggest problem right now.

When you feel the urge to arrange the markers in that specific pattern or repeat what someone just said — does it feel like something you *have* to do to relieve tension or anxiety, or does it feel more like something happening to you that you can't control, even though you don't want it to happen?

I don't... it's not like I'm anxious and trying to fix it. It's just... happening. I'll just be in the middle of a lesson, or one of those art-fair meetings, and I'll just... stop. And then I'm moving the markers around, or getting the papers lined up just right. Or I'll just say back what someone else just said. 

I don't want to do it. It just... happens. And then everyone is looking at me, and I'm not doing what I'm supposed to be doing. It's just... very embarrassing.

When you're arranging the markers or repeating what someone said, do you feel like your own mind is making you do it, or does it feel more like your body is just... doing it on its own, like it's not really coming from you?

I don't know... it's hard to explain. It's just... I'll be in the middle of teaching, or at one of those art-fair meetings, and I just stop. 

I'm not thinking about doing it. I just catch myself doing it... moving the markers, or making the papers sit in that exact pattern. Or I just hear myself repeating the words the other person said instead of answering them. 

It just happens. And it stops me from doing my job... which is embarrassing. I don't really want to talk about it anymore.

When you repeat what someone says or arrange the markers, does it feel like it's coming from your own thoughts and intentions, or does it feel more like something is making your body do it against your will?

I... I don't think anything else is making me do it. It's not like that. 

I just... like I said, I'll be in a lesson, and I just stop what I'm doing to put the markers or the papers in that pattern. Or I repeat the phrase. I don't plan it, it just... happens. And it interrupts my work. 

I really don't want to keep going over this. I already told you what happens, and... it's just very embarrassing.
